# AstroHealth AI – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

AstroHealth AI is a smart, AI-assisted native Android application designed to support astronauts in monitoring and evaluating their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. Space exploration is one of the most challenging areas of modern science and technology because astronauts work in an environment that is very different from Earth. During space missions, they may experience exposure to space radiation, isolation, confinement, altered gravity, limited medical assistance, and changes in their daily routines. These environmental conditions can affect their physical health, psychological well-being, and overall performance. Long-duration missions may contribute to cardiovascular changes, bone density loss, muscle weakness, sleep disturbances, psychological stress, and behavioral health concerns. Therefore, astronauts need reliable tools that help them monitor their health, recognize unusual changes, and make informed decisions about their well-being.

The main purpose of AstroHealth AI is to provide a centralized digital platform where astronauts can record, monitor, and evaluate their important health information. The application combines physical health tracking, mental wellness assessment, sleep monitoring, exercise tracking, health reports, notifications, and AI-assisted risk analysis in one mobile application. It is developed as a native Android application using Kotlin.

ASTROHEALTH AI

Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring System

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Project Documentation

1. Project Overview

AstroHealth AI is an intelligent native Android application designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. The application focuses on monitoring physical health indicators, behavioral wellness, sleep patterns, cardiovascular activity, and exercise routines in challenging space environments.

Astronauts experience several health-related challenges during space missions, including space radiation exposure, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, bone density loss, cardiovascular changes, sleep disturbances, and psychological stress. These conditions can affect their physical performance, mental well-being, and overall health.

AstroHealth AI provides a centralized digital platform that enables astronauts to record, monitor, evaluate, and understand their health information. It combines health tracking, wellness assessments, AI-assisted risk analysis, visual reports, notifications, and offline data storage in one mobile application.

The primary purpose of AstroHealth AI is to help astronauts become more aware of changes in their health and support informed health-related decisions during long-duration space missions.

2. Problem Statement

Long-duration space missions create unique physical and psychological challenges for astronauts. Exposure to space radiation, microgravity, isolation, confinement, and changes in the space environment can contribute to several health concerns.

These concerns include:

  • Cardiovascular changes.
  • Bone density and muscle loss.
  • Changes in sleep patterns.
  • Psychological stress and emotional difficulties.
  • Behavioral health problems.
  • Changes in physical activity and overall fitness.

During long missions, astronauts carry significant responsibility for recognizing changes in their own health. However, monitoring different health indicators separately can make it difficult to understand their overall health condition.

There is a need for an integrated and accessible health monitoring solution that collects important health indicators, organizes personal health records, identifies unusual patterns, and helps astronauts evaluate their well-being.

AstroHealth AI aims to address this challenge through a smart Android-based health monitoring system.

3. Proposed Solution

AstroHealth AI proposes a centralized mobile health monitoring application for astronauts.

The application provides an interactive dashboard where astronauts can review their physical health information, mental wellness assessments, sleep records, exercise activities, and health history.

Users can manually enter health measurements or use simulated demonstration readings when physical monitoring devices are unavailable.

The application analyzes available information through configurable health assessment rules and AI-assisted analysis where implemented. It identifies unusual readings and displays understandable risk indicators.

The system also supports offline access to previously stored health information, making it useful in environments where internet connectivity may be limited.

4. Project Objectives

The major objectives of AstroHealth AI are:

  1. Develop a native Android application for astronaut health monitoring.
  2. Monitor important physical health indicators.
  3. Track sleep duration and sleep quality.
  4. Support mental wellness assessments.
  5. Monitor exercise and physical activity.
  6. Support awareness of bone and cardiovascular health.
  7. Identify unusual health readings and concerning patterns.
  8. Provide health alerts and general recommendations.
  9. Maintain organized daily and weekly health records.
  10. Provide offline access to previously saved health information.
  11. Improve astronaut awareness of physical and behavioral health.
  12. Support proactive health monitoring during long-duration space missions.
5. Target Users

The primary target users include:

  • Astronauts participating in long-duration space missions.
  • Space mission health monitoring teams.
  • Aerospace medical researchers.
  • Researchers studying human health in microgravity.
  • Organizations interested in astronaut wellness and health monitoring.
6. Main Application Modules

6.1 Splash Screen and Application Branding

The application starts with a professional splash screen displaying the AstroHealth AI logo and application name.

The design follows a futuristic space-inspired theme with dark navy blue, neon cyan, and white colors.

The custom logo represents an astronaut, Earth, orbital elements, and a heartbeat symbol.

6.2 Astronaut Profile Module

This module maintains personal astronaut information.

Information includes:

  • Astronaut name.
  • Astronaut identification number.
  • Mission name.
  • Mission duration.
  • Basic profile information.

The profile connects the astronaut with their personal health records.

6.3 Health Monitoring Dashboard

The health dashboard is the central screen of the application.

It displays a summarized view of important health indicators.

Dashboard components include:

  • Current recorded heart rate.
  • Blood oxygen saturation.
  • Body temperature.
  • Sleep duration.
  • Daily physical activity.
  • Mental wellness status.
  • Health risk indicators.
  • Recent health alerts.

The dashboard uses cards, graphs, and visual indicators to make health information easy to understand.

6.4 Heart Rate Monitoring

The heart rate module allows astronauts to record and review heart rate measurements.

The application displays readings in beats per minute (BPM).

Main functions:

  • Record heart rate.
  • Display recent readings.
  • Maintain historical records.
  • Display changes through charts.
  • Highlight readings outside configured demonstration thresholds.

6.5 Blood Oxygen Monitoring

This module records blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) information.

Main functions:

  • Enter oxygen saturation readings.
  • Display recorded oxygen levels.
  • Maintain historical readings.
  • Highlight unusual values.
  • Display health-related warning messages when configured thresholds are crossed.

6.6 Body Temperature Tracking

The body temperature module allows astronauts to record their temperature.

The system stores measurements with dates and times and displays historical temperature information.

Users can review changes in recorded temperature over time.

6.7 Sleep Monitoring Module

Sleep is an important factor in maintaining astronaut performance and overall wellness.

This module allows astronauts to record:

  • Total sleep duration.
  • Sleep quality.
  • Sleep-related observations.
  • Daily and weekly sleep history.

The application can display sleep trends and provide general sleep routine reminders.

6.8 Mental Wellness Assessment

Long-duration missions can involve isolation, confinement, and psychological pressure.

The mental wellness module allows astronauts to complete daily self-assessments.

Assessment components include:

  • Mood selection.
  • Stress level.
  • Emotional well-being.
  • Sleep quality.
  • Daily wellness notes.

The application maintains historical assessments and helps users recognize changes in their reported mental wellness.

6.9 Bone Health and Exercise Tracking

Microgravity can contribute to bone and muscle loss.

This module supports physical activity awareness through exercise tracking.

Features include:

  • Daily exercise records.
  • Exercise duration.
  • Activity history.
  • Exercise reminders.
  • Bone-health-related activity tracking.
  • Weekly activity summaries.

The application encourages astronauts to maintain regular physical activity during space missions.

6.10 Cardiovascular Health Support

This module organizes heart rate and physical activity information to support cardiovascular health awareness.

It displays recorded readings and historical trends.

The purpose is to help astronauts review their cardiovascular-related health information and recognize unusual changes.

6.11 AI-Assisted Health Risk Assessment

AstroHealth AI includes an AI-assisted health assessment concept to analyze available health information.

The module evaluates recorded readings and identifies potentially concerning patterns.

The application can categorize assessment results as:

  • Low Risk.
  • Moderate Risk.
  • High Risk.

It can display general recommendations based on available data.

Examples:

  • Review unusual heart rate readings.
  • Check oxygen measurements.
  • Maintain regular sleep routines.
  • Follow recommended exercise schedules.
  • Seek appropriate medical guidance when concerning patterns appear.

The assessment must be transparent and must not claim to provide a medical diagnosis.

If machine learning is not implemented, use clearly described rule-based assessment instead of claiming a trained AI model.

6.12 Health Alerts and Notifications

The notification module provides reminders and alerts related to recorded health information.

Features include:

  • Unusual reading notifications.
  • Sleep reminders.
  • Exercise reminders.
  • Daily wellness check-in reminders.
  • Health assessment notifications.

Alerts should explain why attention may be required and should not create unnecessary alarm.

6.13 Health Reports and Data Visualization

The reporting module provides organized health summaries.

It includes:

  • Daily health reports.
  • Weekly health reports.
  • Heart rate charts.
  • Oxygen level history.
  • Temperature history.
  • Sleep trends.
  • Exercise activity summaries.
  • Mental wellness history.

Graphs and visualizations help astronauts understand changes in their recorded health information.

6.14 Offline Health Record Management

Space missions may experience communication limitations and internet connectivity problems.

AstroHealth AI supports offline access to previously saved health records through local data storage.

The application should allow users to:

  • Save health measurements locally.
  • Access previously recorded information.
  • Review historical health records.
  • Continue manual health entries without internet access.

Room Database is proposed for local storage.

7. Artificial Intelligence Integration

Artificial intelligence can improve the application's ability to evaluate health information.

The AI-assisted component is designed to identify unusual patterns across recorded health indicators.

Potential analysis areas include:

  • Heart rate variations.
  • Oxygen level changes.
  • Sleep pattern changes.
  • Stress assessment trends.
  • Exercise activity patterns.

The system can use available information to generate understandable risk indicators and general wellness recommendations.

For the initial prototype, configurable rule-based assessment can be used. A trained machine learning model can be introduced in future versions after obtaining suitable validated datasets.

8. Data Collection and Processing

AstroHealth AI supports two initial methods of collecting health information:

Manual Data Entry

Astronauts can enter their health measurements directly into the application.

Simulated Demonstration Data

Sample readings can be used to demonstrate the application's monitoring and reporting functionality when actual sensors are unavailable.

All simulated readings must be clearly marked as DEMO DATA.

The application must not represent sample data as real astronaut measurements.

Future versions may support integration with wearable monitoring devices and compatible biometric sensors.

9. Technology Stack

The proposed technology stack includes:

Programming Language: Kotlin

Development Environment: Android Studio

User Interface: Jetpack Compose

Local Database: Room Database

Application Architecture: MVVM

Data Visualization: Android-compatible charting components

Notifications: Android Notification Manager

AI Assessment: Rule-based analysis initially, with future machine learning integration.

Platform: Native Android

The project must not use Flutter or React Native.

10. Application Design and Theme

AstroHealth AI follows a modern space-inspired medical technology design.

Color palette:

  • Dark Navy Blue: #06152E
  • Neon Cyan: #00D9FF
  • White: #FFFFFF
  • Light Blue: #A7E8FF

Design requirements:

  • Modern and professional interface.
  • Custom astronaut health monitoring logo.
  • Consistent typography.
  • Interactive health dashboard.
  • Rounded information cards.
  • Clear navigation.
  • Readable health indicators.
  • Responsive Android layouts.
  • Professional charts and graphs.

The application logo should be displayed on the splash screen and Android launcher icon.

11. Database Structure

The application should maintain organized local records.

Proposed database entities:

Astronaut Profile

  • Profile ID.
  • Astronaut name.
  • Astronaut ID.
  • Mission name.
  • Mission duration.

Health Records

  • Record ID.
  • Heart rate.
  • SpO2.
  • Body temperature.
  • Recording date.
  • Recording time.

Sleep Records

  • Sleep record ID.
  • Sleep duration.
  • Sleep quality.
  • Recording date.

Wellness Records

  • Wellness record ID.
  • Mood.
  • Stress level.
  • Wellness notes.
  • Recording date.

Exercise Records

  • Exercise ID.
  • Activity type.
  • Duration.
  • Recording date.

Health Alerts

  • Alert ID.
  • Alert category.
  • Alert description.
  • Risk level.
  • Alert date.
12. Application Navigation

The proposed application navigation structure includes:

  1. Splash Screen.
  2. Astronaut Profile.
  3. Main Dashboard.
  4. Physical Health Monitoring.
  5. Mental Wellness.
  6. Sleep Tracking.
  7. Bone and Exercise Tracking.
  8. AI Health Assessment.
  9. Notifications.
  10. Health History and Reports.
  11. Settings.

Each module should be accessible through clear navigation controls.

13. Testing and Quality Assurance

The application should be tested to ensure that its main features work correctly.

Testing activities include:

  • Application launch testing.
  • Navigation testing.
  • Profile input validation.
  • Health data entry testing.
  • Database storage testing.
  • Offline functionality testing.
  • Chart and report testing.
  • Notification testing.
  • Risk assessment testing.
  • Error handling.
  • Android compatibility testing.

The application should not display incorrect health readings or claim that simulated data is real.

14. Security and Privacy

Health information is sensitive and should be handled carefully.

The application should:

  • Store records securely.
  • Avoid unnecessary collection of personal information.
  • Validate user input.
  • Avoid exposing health records.
  • Use appropriate access controls.
  • Clearly identify simulated readings.
  • Protect local health information.
15. Expected Outcomes

The expected outcome is a functional Android prototype that demonstrates how astronauts can monitor and evaluate their health information during long-duration space missions.

AstroHealth AI aims to improve health awareness, organize health records, encourage regular wellness assessments, support physical activity, and help users recognize potentially concerning changes.

The application provides a centralized and accessible platform for reviewing physical and behavioral health information.

16. Innovation and Uniqueness

The main innovation of AstroHealth AI is the integration of physical health monitoring and behavioral wellness assessment in one mobile application.

Unlike a basic health tracker, the proposed application brings together:

  • Physical health indicators.
  • Mental wellness assessments.
  • Sleep monitoring.
  • Exercise and bone-health activity tracking.
  • AI-assisted health risk analysis.
  • Offline health record management.
  • Visual health reporting.

This integrated approach is designed around the specific challenges of long-duration space missions.

17. Future Scope

Future versions of AstroHealth AI may include:

  • Real-time wearable sensor integration.
  • Advanced machine learning models.
  • Space radiation exposure record integration.
  • Improved bone health monitoring.
  • Secure communication with authorized medical teams.
  • Advanced health trend prediction.
  • Integration with validated space medicine datasets.
  • Enhanced astronaut wellness support.
18. NASA Space Apps Challenge Alignment

AstroHealth AI directly addresses the challenge of creating health monitoring software for astronauts on space missions.

The application focuses on helping astronauts gather health indicators, evaluate their physical and behavioral health, recognize unusual changes, and take appropriate action.

It addresses the challenge areas of cardiovascular health, bone health, sleep, mental wellness, isolation, and the need for independent health monitoring during long-duration missions.

By combining mobile technology, health data visualization, offline record management, and AI-assisted analysis, AstroHealth AI proposes an accessible approach to astronaut health monitoring.

19. Conclusion

AstroHealth AI is a proposed native Android health monitoring application developed to support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

The project combines physical health tracking, mental wellness assessment, sleep monitoring, exercise tracking, health alerts, and organized health reporting in one platform.

Its offline-first approach helps maintain access to recorded health information when internet connectivity is limited.

Through its integrated features and space-focused design, AstroHealth AI aims to support astronauts in understanding their health status and making informed decisions about their well-being.

The project demonstrates how native Android development and intelligent health data analysis can contribute to future space exploration and astronaut wellness.
